group: hasTypeValidator - when a TypeValidator is present

cases.description: A JsonSchema instance is spied and its protected getTypeValidator() method is stubbed to return a non‑null mock TypeValidator. The hasTypeValidator() method should return true because a type validator exists.

group: hasTypeValidator - when no TypeValidator is present

cases.description: A JsonSchema instance is spied and its protected getTypeValidator() method is stubbed to return null. The hasTypeValidator() method should return false because there is no type validator.

group: hasTypeValidator - real schema with explicit type keyword

cases.description: A JsonSchema is created from a JSON schema that contains a top‑level "type" keyword. The internal TypeValidator should be instantiated, therefore hasTypeValidator() must return true.

group: hasTypeValidator - real schema without any type keyword

cases.description: The schema defines properties but does not declare a top‑level "type". JsonSchema should not create a TypeValidator for the root schema, so hasTypeValidator() should return false.

group: hasTypeValidator - schema with $ref pointing to a schema that has a type

cases.description: The root schema only contains a $ref that resolves to a definition with a "type" keyword. After resolution, the root JsonSchema should have a TypeValidator, so hasTypeValidator() returns true.

group: hasTypeValidator - schema with $ref pointing to a schema without a type

cases.description: The $ref resolves to a definition that does not declare a top‑level "type" (only nested property types). The root JsonSchema therefore lacks a TypeValidator and hasTypeValidator() must return false.

group: hasTypeValidator - schema with empty type array

cases.description: An empty array for the "type" keyword means no allowed types. The library treats this as the absence of a usable TypeValidator, so hasTypeValidator() should return false.

group: hasTypeValidator - schema with multiple types (array with values)

cases.description: When "type" is an array containing at least one valid type, the JsonSchema creates a composite TypeValidator. Hence hasTypeValidator() returns true.
Calling hasTypeValidator() on a null JsonSchema reference should throw NullPointerException as per Java semantics.

group: hasTypeValidator - schema with invalid type value

cases.description: The "type" keyword must be a string or an array. Supplying a numeric value makes the schema invalid; during schema creation the library throws JsonSchemaException, which propagates when hasTypeValidator() is invoked.
A $ref that resolves to itself creates an infinite recursion during schema resolution. When hasTypeValidator() triggers getTypeValidator(), the recursive resolution eventually overflows the stack.
Creating a JsonSchema with a null JsonNode for the schema and then invoking hasTypeValidator() leads to a NullPointerException inside getTypeValidator() when it attempts to read the "type" property.
